newsitem.title: USA: U.S. students show improved math scores - report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. students show improved math scores - report.

text.p: U.S. students have improved in math achievement over the last six years, but still do not measure up to the highest international standards, the Education Department reported on Thursday.
Overall, results of the 1996 Mathematics Report Card showed that students in fourth, eighth and 12th grade showed continued improvement from 1990 to 1996.
Average math scores rose for white, black and Hispanic students in grades 4 and 12 and for white students in grade 8, the report found.

But Education Secretary Richard Riley said in a statement that American students should aim for the same proficiency in math shown by the First In the World Consortium, a group of Chicago-area eighth-graders who placed second in an international math test, surpassed only by Singapore among 41 nations.

"About half of these consortium students take algebra and geometry by the end of the eighth grade, compared to 20 percent of eighth graders nationally who take algebra," Riley said. "We need to notch our standards higher. If students in other countries are ready for algebra by the eighth grade, why not our students?"
